# v1.1.0-dev.78 — Headers over their columns, corners actually round

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.77`.

## The Monitor And Desktop Headers Were In The Wrong Place

They sat to the right of the numbers they name. That turned out to be
arithmetic rather than a nudge.

The header row and the data rows are separate grids, so a column set to
size-to-content resolves independently in each. The header's Edit cell
is empty and every data row's holds a button — so that column came out
0px wide in the header and 52.125px wide in the rows, and the flexible
name column absorbed the difference. Measured before the fix: both
headers sat exactly 52.1px to the right of their columns.

Every column is a fixed width now except the name, so the two grids
can't disagree. The Edit and History buttons fill their columns, which
lines their edges up down the table as well.

## The Corners Really Are Round Now

The previous release asked for rounded corners with Electron's
`roundedCorners` option. That option is macOS-only — on Windows it does
nothing at all, which is why the corners stayed square.

On Windows 11 the rounding is a DWM window attribute, and a frameless
window doesn't get it by default. The app window and every dialog now
ask for it directly. Windows 10 declines, correctly, since it has no
rounded corners to give.

## Windows Terminal Is Out Of Companion Software

Removed from the catalog. The remaining entries — PowerToys, the
virtual display drivers, PowerShell 7 — are unchanged, and the update
check no longer reports on it.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
